simple.meaning: גַּלְעֵד (Galʻêd) is a Hebrew word meaning “Galed , a memorial cairn East of the Jordan.” BibleIQ connects the English word back to this source word so its use can be compared across Scripture.
simple.biblicalBackground: גַּלְעֵד (H1567) appears 2 times in the Hebrew Bible, beginning at Genesis 31:47, with occurrences in Genesis.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to גַּלְעֵד (H1567) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: English translations can use the same English word for different Hebrew words. BibleIQ anchors the study in גַּלְעֵד (H1567) before moving outward to related references.
simple.summary: גַּלְעֵד (Galʻêd) / H1567 is traced through Genesis 31:47, Genesis 31:48 using source-language evidence and occurrence comparison.

definitions.full: H1567. Galed גַּלְעֵד proper name, of a location ( witness-pile ) name of pile of stones erected by Jacob and his company (Kit Geschichte.129 ; by Laban We Di) Gen 31:47-48 , (see גַּל 1c ) apparently intended to explain גִּלְעָד q. v.; Di conjecture also (as name of altar) Josh 22:34 (compare ᵑ6 ).
